catalyst.event: Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair, at Jackson Lake Lodge, three weeks before the September 16 FOMC. Contract resolves on the 09-16 decision.
catalyst.action: Enter before 08-28 10:00 ET. Trim half on any move above 55c in the hours after the speech; do not wait for resolution if the repricing happens.

thesis: The market prices a September hike at 32c. I estimate 45-50%, and the gap is a decay story rather than a data story. At Warsh's debut FOMC in June the committee held but stripped the easing bias from the statement and NINE OF EIGHTEEN participants projected a 2026 hike; rate futures immediately priced roughly 70% odds for September. Those odds have since halved to 32% while the evidence a hawk would cite has strengthened, not weakened: the 30-year Treasury yield is at its highest since 2007, gold, silver and bitcoin are melting up together, and unemployment FELL to 4.1% from 4.2%. FRED's 2-year at 4.19% against a 3.63% effective funds rate already carries a 56bp hiking premium. With only three meetings left in 2026, nine dots have to be wrong for 32c to be right.
key_risk: Warsh may simply not talk about September. The published Jackson Hole theme this year is financial innovation, payments and policy — not the policy path — so the keynote can pass without a signal and the contract bleeds toward its 09-16 resolution with no catalyst to reprice it. A soft August CPI before the meeting kills the thesis outright.
counter_argument: The odds fell from 70% to 32% for a legitimate reason, not through inattention: the monthly CPI prints have been soft (FRED's July CPI index rose only 0.074% on the month, well under a 2% annual pace). If realised inflation is decelerating, a chair committed to a strict 2% target has no reason to hike, and the metals melt-up is about fiscal supply and term premium rather than about consumer prices — which is exactly the distinction a Fed chair is trained to make. This is why the position is 2% and conviction 3, not 4.

thesis: Dollar General trades at 123.41, 22.0% below its 150-day high of 158.23, wedged between a 20-day at 124.15 and a 50-day at 120.27 — a coiled range into a dated catalyst. The setup is a genuine two-sided consumer read: TJX, the off-price trade-down winner, just collapsed to a 150-day low on its own results, which either means the consumer is weak enough that discounters gain share (DG bullish) or that discretionary retail demand is broadly deteriorating (DG bearish). Dollar General is the purest trade-down expression in US retail — consumables are roughly 80% of its mix — so its comp on 08-27 is the cleanest available test, and a 2.06 EPS print on $11.53B answers it directly.
key_risk: Buying a retailer three days after the sector's most respected operator broke to a 150-day low on earnings is buying into an active de-rating. With a 2.84% ATR, an 08-27 gap can clear both the 119 limit and the 111 stop in the same session — which is why the instruction is to wait for the print rather than to rest a limit order through it. Shrink and wage inflation have repeatedly been the way DG specifically misses.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that DG's problem has never been the consumer — it has been execution: inventory shrink, store conditions and labour cost, all of which broke earnings repeatedly through 2024-2025 in tapes where the trade-down thesis was equally intact. If that is the binding constraint again, a weak consumer does not help DG at all, it just moves market share to Walmart. That is why this is conviction 3, entered after the print, at 2%.

catalyst.event: FDA PDUFA action date for UX111 (rebisufligene etisparvovec), an AAV9 gene therapy seeking accelerated approval for Sanfilippo syndrome type A. If approved it is the FIRST therapy ever approved for the disease.
catalyst.action: Enter before 09-19 in the 24.00-26.50 zone. Trim half into any run above 32 before the date. Do not add in the final week — pre-PDUFA run-ups are where the crowd pays for the privilege.

thesis: The asymmetry here is in the nature of the earlier rejection. UX111 received a Complete Response Letter in July 2025 that was specific to chemistry, manufacturing and controls — the FDA did not dispute efficacy or safety. The resubmission answers those CMC observations and adds up to eight years of follow-up showing durable CSF-HS reduction and continued functional improvement against natural history; the FDA accepted it and set an action date of 2026-09-19. A CMC-only CRL is the most resolvable category of rejection there is, because the agency has already been persuaded the drug works. Meanwhile the stock sits at 25.83, 29.4% below its 150-day high of 36.57, right on its 20-day (25.94) and below its 50-day (28.33) — the date is four weeks out and is not being paid for.
key_risk: This is a binary with a 5.84% ATR, and the 21.50 stop is decoration on 09-19: a second CRL gaps the stock through it in the pre-market with no chance to exit at the level. The stop protects only against drift in the four weeks before the date. Size accordingly — 2% is the ceiling, and the honest way to hold this is as a defined loss of the full 2%, not as a stopped position. Gene therapy manufacturing is also exactly the area where the FDA has been least predictable, and a repeat CMC deficiency is the specific failure mode.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a CMC CRL means the FDA already inspected this manufacturing process once and did not like it, and process remediation for an AAV9 gene therapy is genuinely hard — the base rate for clean second-pass CMC approval is good but not the 80%+ the market's complacency implies. Sanfilippo A is also an ultra-rare indication, so even a clean approval delivers modest revenue and the re-rating has to come from platform credibility rather than from this drug's sales. That is why the target is the 150-day high rather than something dramatic, and why half comes off into any run-up.

instrument: Fed hikes 25bp at the September 16 2026 FOMC — Robinhood 'Fed rate decision in September 2026'

entry.condition: Enter BEFORE the two tests land: core PCE on 08-25/08-26 at 08:30 ET, then Warsh at 10:00 ET on 08-28. The point is to own the option on those events, not to react to them.

exit.scale_plan: If Warsh explicitly signals September on 08-28, sell half into the repricing rather than holding to the 09-16 resolution — this market printed roughly 70% on his June signal alone, so most of the move is available without taking resolution risk.

catalyst.event: Two dated tests inside eight days: July core PCE at 08:30 ET on 08-25 or 08-26 (consensus +0.2% m/m; previews state plainly that a hot print lifts September hike odds), then Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair at 10:00 ET on Friday 08-28. The contract itself resolves on the 09-16 FOMC decision.
catalyst.action: Enter before 08-28 10:00 ET. Trim half on any move above 55c in the hours after the speech; do not wait for resolution if the repricing happens first.

thesis: The market prices a September hike at 32c; I estimate 45-50%, and the gap is a decay story rather than a data story. At Warsh's debut FOMC in June the committee held but stripped the easing bias from its statement, and NINE OF EIGHTEEN participants projected a 2026 hike — rate futures immediately priced roughly 70% odds for September. Those odds have since halved while the evidence a hawk would cite got stronger, not weaker: the 30-year Treasury yield is at its highest since 2007, gold, silver and bitcoin are melting up together, and unemployment FELL to 4.1% from 4.2%. FRED's 2-year at 4.19% against a 3.63% effective funds rate already embeds a 56bp hiking premium. With three meetings left in 2026, nine dots have to be wrong for 32c to be right. Venue verified: Robinhood lists this event as 'Fed rate decision in September 2026' and shows 69% on the maintain-rate leg, consistent with the 32c hike price.
key_risk: Warsh may simply not address September. The published Jackson Hole theme is financial innovation, payments and policy — not the policy path — so the keynote can pass without a signal, leaving the contract to bleed toward resolution with no catalyst to reprice it. A soft core PCE print this week kills the thesis outright, and it lands first.
counter_argument: The odds fell from 70% to 32% for a legitimate reason rather than through inattention: monthly inflation has been soft, with FRED's July CPI index up only 0.074% on the month, well under a 2% annual pace. If realised inflation is decelerating, a chair committed to a strict 2% target has no reason to hike, and the metals melt-up is about fiscal supply and term premium rather than consumer prices — exactly the distinction a Fed chair is trained to draw. Note also that the 'number of rate cuts in 2026' market sits at 88% for zero cuts, which means the hold-not-hike outcome is already the consensus and well-examined. That is why this is 2% at conviction 3, not a larger bet.
